sourceNotes: Seeded from ENT roleplay performance indicators and entrepreneurship cluster exam data.
Terms are scoped for future vocab-card, quiz, and event-filter UI use.

terms.definition: The clear reason a customer should choose one business, product, or service instead of a competitor.
terms.whyItMatters: ENT roleplays often ask competitors to identify what makes a new venture meaningfully different.

terms.definition: The process of defining the specific group of customers a business is trying to reach.
terms.whyItMatters: Helps competitors justify who the business should serve before choosing products, services, or promotions.

terms.definition: The full set of products and services a business offers to customers.
terms.whyItMatters: ENT scenarios frequently ask whether the current mix should expand, contract, or shift for a new customer base.

terms.definition: A strategy that adds new items to an existing product line.
terms.whyItMatters: Useful when recommending new merchandise, add-ons, or service options for an entrepreneurial venture.

terms.definition: The expectation a brand sets for customers about the value and experience it will consistently deliver.
terms.whyItMatters: Strong ENT answers connect proposed services or policies back to the promise the business wants to own.

terms.definition: Any interaction where a customer or potential customer encounters a brand.
terms.whyItMatters: Touchpoints help explain how ads, websites, store layouts, staff, products, and reviews shape brand image.

terms.definition: How a business wants customers to perceive its product, service, or brand compared with alternatives.
terms.whyItMatters: Positioning links customer service, product mix, pricing, and promotion into one competitive image.

terms.definition: A description of an ideal or likely customer using traits such as demographics, interests, needs, and behavior.
terms.whyItMatters: Profiles make recommendations more specific than saying a business should target everyone.

terms.definition: The customer group a business chooses as the main audience for its marketing and sales efforts.
terms.whyItMatters: Most ENT roleplays expect a clear target before competitors recommend products, channels, or messages.

terms.definition: A study of a market segment to evaluate customer need, ability to buy, access, and opportunity.
terms.whyItMatters: Market analysis supports evidence-based recommendations instead of guesses.

terms.definition: The organized collection and interpretation of information about customers, competitors, and market conditions.
terms.whyItMatters: ENT competitors can use research to turn customer feedback or survey data into business recommendations.

terms.definition: A specific recommendation that a business can realistically act on using available resources.
terms.whyItMatters: Judges reward analysis that turns data into a concrete next step.

terms.definition: The path a product or service takes from the producer or provider to the final customer.
terms.whyItMatters: Channel choices affect convenience, cost, customer reach, and the buying experience.

terms.definition: A plan for choosing and managing the channels a business will use to deliver products or services.
terms.whyItMatters: Entrepreneurs use channel strategy to decide between direct sales, online ordering, retailers, partners, or hybrid access.

terms.definition: Communication used to inform, persuade, or remind customers about a business, product, service, or idea.
terms.whyItMatters: ENT scenarios often require choosing the right promotional message and channel for a specific market.

terms.definition: Activities that build and maintain a positive relationship between an organization and its publics.
terms.whyItMatters: PR vocabulary helps competitors discuss press, community trust, reputation, and service recovery.

terms.definition: Unpaid media or public attention that can help or hurt a business's reputation.
terms.whyItMatters: Knowing publicity versus paid advertising makes promotional recommendations more precise.

terms.definition: A written plan that sets marketing goals, strategies, tactics, budgets, and measures of success.
terms.whyItMatters: A marketing plan gives roleplay recommendations structure and makes them easier to evaluate.

terms.definition: The broad approach a business uses to reach customers and achieve marketing goals.
terms.whyItMatters: Strategy explains why a tactic fits the customer, business goal, and competitive situation.

terms.definition: The money, equipment, facilities, and other assets needed to start or operate a venture.
terms.whyItMatters: ENT competitors often must explain what resources a recommendation requires and whether the cost is justified.

terms.definition: The process of creating, funding, launching, and beginning operations for a new business.
terms.whyItMatters: Start-up language helps explain funding, feasibility, resource needs, and early operating choices.

terms.definition: Ongoing business costs that are not tied directly to producing one unit of a product or service.
terms.whyItMatters: Cost awareness helps competitors judge whether a proposed service or product mix is sustainable.

terms.definition: An economic system in which individuals and businesses own resources and pursue profit with limited government control.
terms.whyItMatters: Entrepreneurship exams often connect profit, competition, and risk to private enterprise.

terms.definition: The desire to earn profit, which encourages people to invest, start businesses, and take business risks.
terms.whyItMatters: This is a core economics term behind entrepreneurial decision-making.

terms.definition: Planning, developing, marketing, and managing offerings across their life.
terms.whyItMatters: It ensures offerings meet customer needs and generate sustainable revenue.

terms.definition: A person who spots an opportunity and creates, owns, and runs a new venture.
terms.whyItMatters: Entrepreneurship events center on the owner's role in decisions and strategy.

terms.definition: Facts and figures that have been processed into a meaningful, usable form for decisions.
terms.whyItMatters: Competitors must know that raw data becomes useful only once it is organized and interpreted.

terms.definition: The process of creating, communicating, and delivering value to customers.
terms.whyItMatters: This is the umbrella concept behind many cluster and roleplay decisions.

terms.definition: The stock of goods or materials a business holds for sale or use.
terms.whyItMatters: Inventory management balances meeting demand against storage cost.

terms.definition: Tangible products in limited supply that must be produced and purchased.
terms.whyItMatters: Distinguishing goods from services underlies every business model.

terms.definition: The stages a product passes through: introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.
terms.whyItMatters: The stage a product is in drives its marketing, pricing, and distribution.

terms.definition: Identifying unmet market needs or underserved customer segments.
terms.whyItMatters: Judges assess how well competitors spot a genuine market need.

terms.definition: Raw, unprocessed facts and figures collected through observation, measurement, or research.
terms.whyItMatters: All information management begins with knowing what counts as reliable data.

terms.definition: Information on customer behavior, market trends, sales, and competitive activity.
terms.whyItMatters: Quality data enables predictive insight and competitive advantage.

terms.definition: A distribution path where a producer sells straight to customers with no intermediaries.
terms.whyItMatters: Direct channels maximize control and margin but demand more sales and logistics effort.

terms.definition: The blend of advertising, publicity, sales promotion, and personal selling.
terms.whyItMatters: A mix lets competitors recommend more than one communication path.

terms.definition: The overall impression customers have of a business or product.
terms.whyItMatters: Image affects trust, loyalty, and perceived value.

terms.definition: A formal document requesting goods or services from a vendor at set terms.
terms.whyItMatters: Purchase orders create the paper trail for efficient procurement.

terms.definition: The inputs — land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship — used to produce goods and services.
terms.whyItMatters: Managing limited resources is central to operations and strategy.

terms.definition: An analysis of whether a business idea is achievable, viable, and sustainable.
terms.whyItMatters: It justifies recommendations and addresses resource constraints.

terms.definition: An organized, computer-managed collection of related data that can be stored and retrieved systematically.
terms.whyItMatters: Businesses run everything from inventory to customer records on databases.

terms.definition: Original data collected firsthand through surveys, interviews, or experiments.
terms.whyItMatters: It gives firsthand customer and market insight for a specific question.

terms.definition: A distribution path where one or more intermediaries sit between producer and customer.
terms.whyItMatters: Indirect channels widen reach and share costs but reduce producer control.

terms.definition: Paid, nonpersonal communication delivered through media to large audiences.
terms.whyItMatters: Advertising builds broad brand awareness efficiently and at scale.

terms.definition: A person who buys and uses goods and services.
terms.whyItMatters: Naming the consumer keeps recommendations grounded in who actually benefits.

terms.definition: A supplier that provides goods or services to a business.
terms.whyItMatters: Vendor choice drives product quality, cost, and supply reliability.

terms.definition: The relationship between how much of a good is available and how much customers want to buy.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains pricing, scarcity, inventory, and opportunity.

terms.definition: A group of related products sold under one brand or category.
terms.whyItMatters: Line decisions balance customer choice against cost and complexity.

terms.definition: Funding a venture from personal savings and reinvested revenue, not outside capital.
terms.whyItMatters: Many scenarios require building a business with limited resources.

terms.definition: A software application that organizes data in rows and columns for calculation and analysis.
terms.whyItMatters: Spreadsheets are a core business tool competitors are expected to use comfortably.
